name: Oregon

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (ORS 702.001 to 702.065)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. Agents for endorsement deals must register. ORS 702.200 lets athletes hire an agent for NIL, and skips the contract warning for those deals.
contract_warning: Warning to the student athlete: If you or your parent or guardian signs this contract: (1) You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport. (2) If you have an athletic director, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director within 72 hours after entering into this contract, or before you participate in any interscholastic or intercollegiate sports event, whichever occurs first, that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent. (3) You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
summary: Register with the Department of Education. $250 plus fingerprints.

steps.text: Fill out the athlete agent application
steps.detail: Sign it in ink and get it notarized. ODE says to send it through its secure Smartsheet upload or the Athlete Agent Portal.
$150 if based on another state's registration.

steps.text: Finish all of it within 30 days
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you contact a minor's parent. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, other pay you get for the deal, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed. Say you're registered in Oregon and list your other states.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student athlete in bold capital letters next to their signature
steps.detail: Use Oregon's set wording. It is not required for an NIL deal covered by ORS 702.200.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: A parent or guardian signs it if the athlete is a minor. It is not required for an NIL deal covered by ORS 702.200.

steps.text: Have a parent or guardian sign the contract if the athlete is a minor
Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the warning when they sign
steps.detail: Give it to the parent if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. Missing this is a felony in Oregon. The athlete (or parent of a minor) may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Tell the new school within 72 hours if your athlete enrolls later
steps.detail: Count from when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Oregon and federal law (SPARTA) ban predating or postdating it.
Each client's name and address, each contract and what you spent to recruit each athlete. ODE may inspect them.

steps.text: Never give an athlete anything of value before they sign, or make false promises
steps.detail: Don't pay anyone else to steer them to you either. Giving gifts is a felony in Oregon.

steps.text: Don't represent an athlete at a school you worked for in the last 4 years
steps.detail: This applies if you represented that college or university in any way.
Registration lasts 2 years. The $150 renewal fee is in ORS 702.023.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: ORS 702.200 covers NIL deals for athletes at Oregon colleges. For those deals the contract warning and separate eligibility warning are not required, but the other rules still apply. Confirm with ODE at athlete@ode.oregon.gov how it reads this.
